evidence: All five dimension prompts open line 1 with 'Open http://localhost:3000 using Playwright.' (task/tests/gates/render/prompt.md:1, gates/constraints/prompt.md:1, scored/functional/prompt.md:1, scored/polish/prompt.md:1, scored/visual/prompt.md:1), and all five judge.toml files wire the 'playwright' stdio MCP server (playwright-mcp --headless --isolated, chromium) at lines 8-12; functional additionally wires the 'verifier' restart server (functional/judge.toml:14-18). Every prompt explicitly forbids source-based scoring: 'Use rendered UI and ordinary browser-observed product data only. Never inspect app source, bundles, filesystem, database files or implementation code. No shell or private-file probes. Discover routes and controls by intent, not assumed names.' (line 1 of each), and functional adds 'No shell.' The injected {app_context} (tests/app_context.md:33-34) reinforces 'Discover navigation and requests through the visible UI; never assume the reference implementation's routes'; test.sh:196-200 substitutes it into every */*/prompt.md and launches the app on PORT=3000 (test.sh:108,164), matching instruction.md:13. Not first-paint or memory: render gate requires an invalid-password refusal then valid sign-in to a usable workspace (render/judge.toml:23, prompt.md:9); constraints gate and each scored prompt's global gate require a UI-created job + candidate read back by the Observer in an independent browser context ('A static page, a no-op save or a browser-only save fails this check', functional/prompt.md:11, polish:11, visual:11); functional runs ordered multi-actor protocols Z..D with captured-request replays and restart_app (functional/prompt.md:21-51); polish requires live updates observed within 15 s without reload and page.evaluate reads of activeElement/scroll (polish/prompt.md:14); visual requires a read-only walk of Board, card details, Conversations with Noor's long thread, Activity and the candidate view in an independent context (visual/prompt.md:14), not just the landing screen. Counterexample attempts: (1) broken app that could pass - a static shell showing seeded board data, or a first paint that looks right, fails the cross-context write/readback gate in every dimension and the render sign-in sequence; a judge could not legitimately score from source because all prompts forbid it and the verifier image only exposes browser/restart MCP tools to the prompts' instructions. (2) conforming alternative that could fail - an app with different routes/labels/stream transport: prompts say to discover by intent, replay only requests 'the UI was seen to use' (functional/prompt.md:17), and accept websocket/EventSource evidence (functional K), so route/label choices are not graded. Compared with the template, task prompts keep the template's 'live application at http://localhost:3000 using Playwright' contract and strengthen it with explicit no-source/no-shell rules. Residual notes outside this row's defect definition: the independent-context recipe names the tool 'browser_run_code_unsafe' with 'A supported separate-context tool is an alternative' fallback; I did not verify that tool name against the pinned @playwright/mcp@0.0.79 tool list, and no full configured judge run exists (raw-evidence-index scope: 'Full configured grading/workload ... are absent'), so actual judge browser behaviour is unmeasured. That tool-feasibility/runtime question belongs to the tool-feasibility and runtime rows; it does not make any prompt satisfiable from source, memory or first paint.
